title: runtime/kv-cache: estimate saved_prefill_ms + hit_bytes accounting (partial-prefill safe)
author: Samir Qureshi
description:
Implements runtime-side accounting for (1) kv-cache hit bytes and (2) a best-effort estimate of prefill latency avoided due to prefix/KV cache hits (saved_prefill_ms). This is part of the v2 cache telemetry sprint (ENG-4814) and unblocks dashboards/alerts + Optimize recommendations that need trustworthy “savings” signals beyond raw hit-rate.

Motivation: current telemetry can tell us that a request was a cache hit/miss, but not how much work was actually avoided. In particular, partial-prefill is common (prompt diverges after a shared prefix), and naive accounting tends to (a) over-count savings on partial hits, or (b) produce negative/unstable values when tokenization or truncation differs between cached and uncached paths.

What this PR adds:
- hit_bytes accounting: emits per-request byte totals for KV entries served from cache (separately for prefill/prefix path), based on the actual number of cached tokens returned by the cache lookup and the model’s KV layout.
- saved_prefill_ms estimation: estimates “milliseconds of prefill compute avoided” as cached_prompt_tokens * prefill_cost_ms_per_token(model, dtype, kv_layout, gpu_class). The estimator is intentionally conservative and saturates to avoid double-counting on partial-prefill.
- partial-prefill correctness: when the request requires some new prefill after a cached prefix, we only attribute savings to the cached tokens (not to any tokens that still ran prefill). If the request is truncated or the cache prefix exceeds the effective prompt length, we clamp to effective_prompt_tokens.
- feature flag: all new fields are behind runtime flag runtime.cache_telemetry_v2_savings (default off). When off, we continue to emit existing counters but do not compute byte/savings estimates.

Key implementation details:
- Cache lookup returns CacheLookupResult { cached_prompt_tokens, cache_line_id, kv_layout_fingerprint, ... }.
- We compute effective_prompt_tokens after tokenization + truncation (post routing/model selection).
- cached_effective_tokens = min(cached_prompt_tokens, effective_prompt_tokens) (clamp).
- hit_bytes = cached_effective_tokens * bytes_per_token_kv(model, kv_layout_fingerprint). bytes_per_token_kv uses runtime model metadata already used by allocator sizing; we do not attempt to infer based on GPU memory allocator state.
- saved_prefill_ms = cached_effective_tokens * prefill_ms_per_token_estimate(model, gpu_class). prefill_ms_per_token_estimate uses a small model table + gpu class bucket (A10/L4/L40S/H100) with sane defaults and “unknown => 0” behavior to avoid bogus savings.
- We store per-request savings in RequestTelemetryContext and export via the structured cache event payload (actual metric mapping/naming is handled in the telemetry pipeline PR).

Testing:
- Unit tests for clamp behavior (cached > prompt, prompt > cached, zero tokens, unknown model metadata).
- Synthetic integration test that forces partial-prefill by varying suffix tokens; asserts that saved_prefill_ms is monotonic in cached tokens and never exceeds total observed prefill time for the request.
- Adds a tiny golden fixture for KV layout byte accounting across a couple of common architectures.

Perf:
- No extra allocations on hot path (uses existing request context + a few integer ops).
- Prefill_ms_per_token_estimate lookup is an O(1) table lookup cached per-model.

Notes / follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Telemetry pipeline will rename and aggregate fields per v2 spec; this PR only adds runtime-side fields.
- Better per-model calibration for prefill_ms_per_token_estimate will come from perf-canary data (ENG-4819).

review_conversation: Omar El-Sayed (review): For partial-prefill, are we guaranteeing saved_prefill_ms can’t exceed the actual observed prefill time? Especially when cache returns tokens but tokenizer truncates downstream (max_prompt_tokens).

Samir Qureshi (author): Yes — cached_effective_tokens is clamped to effective_prompt_tokens which is computed post-tokenization + truncation. Also we added an integration test that asserts saved_prefill_ms <= observed_prefill_ms for the synthetic workload. Note: for unknown gpu_class/model metadata we return 0 to avoid bogus savings.
Noah Patel (review): How stable is bytes_per_token_kv across model versions? If kv_layout_fingerprint changes, could we miscount hit_bytes for older cache lines?

Samir Qureshi (author): We count hit_bytes using the kv_layout_fingerprint returned by the cache lookup for the served cache line. If we can’t resolve that fingerprint to a known layout at runtime (e.g., old cache line), we emit hit_bytes=0 and log once per process (rate-limited). Added unit test for “unknown fingerprint => 0”.
Marcus Reed (review): The prefill_ms_per_token_estimate table makes me nervous—can this produce large swings across GPU SKUs/regions and confuse dashboards?

Samir Qureshi (author): Agreed. The goal here is a conservative estimate to make “savings present vs not present” visible. We bucket by gpu_class (from runtime hardware introspection) and keep default=0. Calibration via perf-canary will refine the table; I also added a cap such that saved_prefill_ms can’t exceed observed_prefill_ms in the integration test. Pipeline/dashboard can also display both hit_bytes and saved_prefill_ms so users can sanity-check.

Logan Wright (review): Telemetry semantics: please make sure these fields are explicitly ‘estimate’ and that units are consistent (ms, bytes). Also confirm we’re not emitting per-request IDs anywhere.

Samir Qureshi (author): Fields are named saved_prefill_ms_estimate and kv_cache_hit_bytes in the structured payload. No request_id added here. Units are ms (float) and bytes (uint64). Metric naming + aggregation will be handled in the telemetry pipeline PR (ENG-4815).
Sofia Ivanova (review): Scheduling interaction: on partial-prefill, prefill may be chunked. Are we attributing savings in a way that could double-count across chunks?

Samir Qureshi (author): Savings are computed once per request from cached_effective_tokens, independent of how prefill is chunked by the scheduler. We only attach it to the cache outcome event emitted during lookup, not per chunk.

Omar El-Sayed (request changes): Please clamp against ‘effective_prompt_tokens’ computed after routing/model selection but before any speculative decode/rollback. Also add a comment explaining why unknown=>0.
Samir Qureshi (author): Done in 8a31f2b — moved clamp to use prompt_tokens_post_truncation from RequestPlan and added comment + test for unknown=>0. Perf smoke rerun passed.
Omar El-Sayed (approve): LGTM after clamp fix and tests. Ship behind flag.
Noah Patel (approve): +1. Conservative unknown=>0 is the right call for now.
release_notes: Runtime: Adds cache savings accounting fields (hit_bytes, saved_prefill_ms estimate) behind runtime.cache_telemetry_v2_savings; improves correctness for partial-prefill/truncation cases.
